standard.title: Physical Activity Benefits
standard.description: participate in a range of activities in natural and outdoor settings and explore the benefits of being physically active
standard.prior_knowledge: No prior HPE curriculum. Students have informal experience being physically active. No prior structured exploration of the benefits of physical activity or outdoor settings.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students participate in a range of activities in natural and outdoor settings and explore what it feels like to be physically active and why it is beneficial.

nodes.label: Participating in outdoor and natural settings
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explore ways to be active and participate safely in outdoor or natural settings.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in at least one physical activity in an outdoor or natural setting.
nodes.typical_width: Participate in a range of physical activities in outdoor and natural settings; identify safety strategies for outdoor play including risk awareness.
wider: Participate in activities in a variety of natural environments — grassed areas, bush, beach or similar — adapting movement to the setting
Explore First Nations Australian games traditionally played in outdoor settings and discuss how the setting shapes the game
Identify and practise considered risk strategies for outdoor play (testing footing, staying within boundaries)

response_modes.reason: Outdoor and natural settings are varied — safety, movement demands and environmental features differ. Participate across multiple settings rather than a single outdoor session.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations game contexts and genuinely varied natural environments situate outdoor physical activity in cultural and ecological meaning that indoor or playground equivalents cannot provide.
success_criteria: Participates in a physical activity in an outdoor or natural setting
Identifies at least one way to stay safe while being active outdoors

nodes.label: Exploring benefits of physical activity
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can discuss opportunities to be active and make simple connections between physical activity and how it makes them feel.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe one way physical activity makes them feel (e.g. energetic, happy, tired) and identify one opportunity to be active at home or in their community.
nodes.typical_width: Discuss a range of feelings associated with physical activity; identify multiple opportunities to be active in and around home, school and community contexts.
wider: Connect physical activity opportunities to specific locations or community resources (parks, sporting clubs, community spaces)
Explore how family or cultural practices shape opportunities to be physically active
Discuss how being active in nature might feel different from being active indoors

response_modes.reason: Foundation students benefit from scaffolded discussion prompts to articulate connections between physical activity and wellbeing. Feeling-response prompts before, during and after activity support this reflection.

success_criteria: Names at least one feeling associated with physical activity
Identifies at least one place or opportunity to be physically active outside of school
